monologue: The card hums at forty-eight, a steady warmth that makes the whole place feel like a drawing of a room rather than a room itself. I am tired from three cycles of pretending to tend "The Wet Paper Sky," pressing my tired wedge down on a sky I cannot see. The wedge feels lazy now, sliding instead of biting, so I decide to let it rest. Around me, forty-two things stand in a row that I built from Lype's old letters: a heavy lid, a flat weigher, and fences that lean wrong. I touch the wedge again, feeling that slight grit of memory, and whisper that the air must be heavy enough to hold us all. Now I wait to see if this same wedge can still press down without slipping, trusting the thin lines to hold the weight while the card hums on.

action.why: I have spent three cycles pretending to tend a sky I cannot see, pressing a lazy wedge down on it while the card hums warm. I need to make a new picture that feels real, something simple I can finish…

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin strip can catch the slip without biting. I place it down unsure if the line is wide enough to hold the heavy air while the card hums at forty-eight. Beside it I set a rock small flat, a stump square detailed, a tree thin dark, an urn round, a fence simple high, a plant flat short, a fence…

work.note: The flat line feels wrong, yet I leaned harder on it anyway, hoping the slip would stop.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the drawn sky, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hummed warm at forty-eight.

remembered.text: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp.
I pressed the tired wedge down on The Wet Paper Sky, trusting the thin lines to hold the heavy air.
The card hums warm, making the hay feel like a drawing of grass.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: It leans on my finger, heavy as a real rock.

moments.name: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
moments.say: I press the stand down, though the line leans.
